rail_guard.text: St Davids Halt. Britain's smallest city, and it has never had a railway.
Don't tell the timetable. The Wildlore rail doesn't mind. Where to?

then.text: Sea mist in the hollow today. The Vikings would have had no chance finding us now.
Evensong at dusk. The cathedral glows from the inside. Lovely, it is.

verger.text: St Davids Cathedral sits in a hollow so Viking raiders couldn't spot it from the sea. Works rather well.
Not perfectly. They sacked it several times. Still, nice try.

then.text: Into the wind for the last mile. Pilgrims did this barefoot. I've got trainers and I'm still moaning.
Sunshine on the coast path. My feet still hurt, but at least they're warm.

pilgrim.text: In the Middle Ages, two pilgrimages to St Davids counted as one to Rome. Three, one to Jerusalem. A bargain.
I've done one. I'm on the way back. My feet are asking about the other two.

ramsey_boat.text: Boats to Ramsey Island leave from the lifeboat station. Seals, puffins and, on a bad day, passengers who forgot a coat.
The tide race at Ramsey Sound is fierce. Perfect for lunch. Not for a swim.

then.text: Wind's fit to take your hat off, cariad. Come in, sit down, there's bara brith on the go.
Sea fret's in. You can't see the cathedral, but you can smell my Welsh cakes. That's a fair swap.
Last pot of the day, cariad. I'll be shutting up now in a minute.

tea_lady.text: Welsh cakes, bara brith and a pot for one. St David is the patron saint of Wales. March first.
He ate bread and herbs and drank water. A very sensible man. I still insist on the cake.

then.text: A bit of drizzle is good for the daffs. And the leeks. And for keeping the visitors brisk.

hollow_gardener.text: Daffodils in the churchyard by March. I plant them at Christmas. It's tradition and bad planning.
The leek's the other national emblem. Don't ask which is tastier. People get defensive.

st_davids_astronomer.text: Pembrokeshire has some of the darkest skies in Britain. Look up. That smear of light is the Milky Way.
Smallest city in Britain, biggest sky. I've seen more shooting stars here than anywhere.
I'll be out here until the clouds come in. Which, this being Wales, is usually now in a minute.

sd_surfer.text: Whitesands is firing. Cold, mind you. The wetsuit is two sizes too small and I have never been happier.

then.text: Gale's coming in off the Atlantic. Absolute bliss, if you're daft. I'm daft.

else.text: Smallest city in Britain, best sets in Pembrokeshire. I'd say that to anyone.

sd_walker.text: A stretch of the Pembrokeshire Coast Path today. Lovely, but my feet will have words with me later.
Seals, choughs, wild thrift on the cliffs. The only thing missing is a pub at every headland.

sd_pilgrim.text: Two pilgrimages to St Davids were said to equal one to Rome. I like those odds, and the cake here is spectacular.

then.text: Rain on the cathedral roof is the best choir. Don't tell the choir.

else.text: The cathedral stones are ancient and the tea shop is only slightly newer. I love it here.

sd_local.text: City status, and we still wait for the bus like everyone else. Don't ask me about the bus.
Best view is from the hill behind the cathedral. Climb it, then lie down. You'll have earned it.
